newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts end higher, bouncing back from Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts end higher, bouncing back from Greenspan.

text.p: 1623 GMT - Gilts end higher as market bounces back from Greenspan-inspired losses, helped by stronger Bunds and steady Treasuries. Market focus turns to key by-election in Wirral South but Labour victory widely discounted.
* March long gilt future settles 18/32 higher at 113-07.

Dealers said a strong recovery by German Bunds had boosted gilts. "Today's rally was a little bit of a bear-squeeze on the back of a strong Germany," the senior salesman said. "But we have also seen some good buying ourselves and switching longer."
Firmer Treasuries had also helped, traders said. "The worry was that we might get another sell-off in T-bonds and that hasn't happened," one said. "That helped gilts."
Attention would now turn to the key by-election in Wirral South, analysts said. A victory for the opposition Labour party has been widely discounted.
"Even if you assume that a Labour victory is bad news, it's already priced in," a trader said.

Some analysts said a narrow Labour majority or a surprise Conservative win could upset gilts by raising the spectre of a hung parliament after Britain's general election, which must be held by May 22.

Although European markets had managed to recover from the impact of Greenspan's warning that pre-emptive U.S. interest rate rises could not be ruled out, they would remain nervous ahead of the second half of his Humphrey Hawkins testimony on Wednesday, traders said.
"The problem we've got from the U.S. is that the second half of Greenspan's speech has been postponed," one said.
"The second part of his testimony has often been used by him as a vehicle to suggest the market's reaction has been overdone or was OK," he said. "So until we get that we could tread water a bit."
With no significant UK data due on Friday, the post by-election focus for gilts would probably be revised U.S. fourth-quarter GDP data at 1330 GMT and the Chicago PMI at 1500 GMT, analysts said.
Spreads against Bunds narrowed slightly, moving in one basis point to 173 in the 10-year area.
Short sterling futures were generally a touch easier, with the March contract unchanged at 93.73 and the June contract one basis point lower at 93.53.
